implementation_notes: Kotlin/JVM realises the multiton the way Java does, with a shorter call: a companion object holds a ConcurrentHashMap<Key, T> (kotlin.collections typealias of java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap) and the stdlib extension ConcurrentMap.getOrPut(key) { create(key) } does the get-or-put-if-absent, documented as safe for concurrent maps. A private constructor plus a companion factory keep construction closed; an object declaration would give a single instance, not a keyed family, so it is the wrong tool here, and the companion object is per class loader like any JVM static.
pitfalls: Plain mutableMapOf + getOrPut is not atomic (the docs say so for maps modified concurrently); a multithreaded registry needs ConcurrentHashMap or a synchronized block.
In the concurrent overload the defaultValue lambda may run even when the key is already present, so construction with side effects that must happen once per key needs computeIfAbsent or a Lazy slot.
The typealias hides the JVM collection: class-loader scoping and the blocking behaviour of computeIfAbsent-style operations are inherited unchanged from java.util.concurrent.
